questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{{x}^{5}},\, & x\ge 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{4}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(-\frac{4}{3{x}^{3}})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\frac{4}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =2-{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{17}{24},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}, & 1\le x, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3{x}^{2}}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}+{(-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}-{(\frac{17}{24})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{143}{576} \\  & ≈0.25\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{20(x-1)}{{x}^{6}},\, & x\ge 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{20(x-1)}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20x-20}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{20}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{20}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{4}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{20(x-1)}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20x-20}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{20}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{20}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{10}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{20}{3{x}^{3}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{10}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{10}{3}-{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{5}{6},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{2}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{5}},\, & x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3x}{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3{x}^{3}}{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{3{x}^{4}}{8}|}_{0}^{1}+(-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}){|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}-{(\frac{5}{6})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{72}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{5}{3},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3}, & 0<x<2 \\ \frac{2(3-x)}{3},\, & 2\le x<3 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2(3-x)}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{6{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{12}|}_{0}^{2}+(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{6}){|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+(18-\frac{27}{2})-(\frac{16}{3}-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+\frac{11}{6} \\  & =\frac{19}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{19}{6}-{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
